title: MATH 115
description: A first calculus course: limits, derivatives and their applications, and an introduction to integrals.
notes: Michigan's official description is in a login-only LSA course guide. The plan calls it 'Mathematics 115', the first course of its calculus sequence; the content is written from that role.

title: MATH 116
description: A second calculus course: techniques and applications of integration, sequences, and series.
notes: Michigan's official description is in a login-only LSA course guide. The plan calls it 'Mathematics 116', the second course of its calculus sequence.

title: MATH 214
description: A linear algebra course with applications: systems of linear equations, matrices, vector spaces, eigenvalues, and their use in engineering and computing.
notes: Michigan's official description is in a login-only LSA course guide. Footnote 1 lists MATH 217, 417, 419, or ROB 101 as alternatives, all linear algebra courses.

title: MATH 215 or MATH 216 (Mathematics 215 or 216)
description: Either a multivariable calculus course (vectors, partial derivatives, multiple integrals) or an introductory differential equations course.
notes: Choice slot: Michigan's MATH 215 or MATH 216. Their official descriptions are in a login-only LSA course guide.

title: ENGR 100
description: A first-year engineering course built around team design projects, with technical communication, engineering ethics, and the role of the engineer in society.
notes: Michigan's ENGR course guide was not saved (Chrome blocked the download in step 13); the plan's title is 'Introduction to Engineering'.

title: ENGR 101
description: An introductory programming course for engineers: algorithms and programming in languages such as C++ and MATLAB, and computing as an engineering tool.
notes: Michigan's ENGR course guide was not saved (Chrome blocked the download in step 13); the plan's title is 'Introduction to Computers'.

title: Chemistry
description: A general chemistry course with laboratory: atomic structure, bonding, reactions, stoichiometry, and the properties of matter.
notes: Michigan: Chemistry 125/126 and 130 or Chemistry 210 and 211.

title: PHYS 140
description: A calculus-based introductory physics course on mechanics, with its laboratory: motion, forces, energy, momentum, and rotation.
notes: Michigan's official description is in a login-only LSA course guide. The plan pairs PHYS 140 with Lab 141, the first of its two physics courses.

title: PHYS 240
description: A calculus-based introductory physics course on electricity and magnetism, with its laboratory: electric fields, circuits, magnetic fields, and induction.
notes: Michigan's official description is in a login-only LSA course guide. The plan pairs PHYS 240 with Lab 241, the second of its two physics courses.

title: Intellectual Breadth
description: Courses in the humanities and social sciences chosen by the student, which add breadth outside engineering and computing.

title: General Electives
description: Any course the student chooses, inside or outside the major, that counts toward the degree. Students often use free electives for a minor, extra courses in the major, or personal interests.

title: Flexible Technical Electives
description: Technical courses chosen from an approved list that can include computer science and supporting fields such as mathematics, science, and engineering.

title: Statistics course
description: A course in probability or statistics: probability models, random variables, and statistical inference such as estimation and hypothesis testing.
notes: Choice slot: one of nine Michigan courses (STATS 250 ... IOE 265). EECS 301's official description is in data/raw/umich/ (courses-eecs page).

title: TCHNCLCM 300
description: A short technical communication course for engineering and computing students, on writing and presenting technical information clearly.
notes: Michigan's TCHNCLCM course guide was not saved (Chrome blocked the download in step 13).

title: Upper Level CS Technical Electives
description: Upper-level computer science courses chosen by the student from approved lists. Common options cover areas such as machine learning, security, operating systems, databases, and software engineering.
notes: Michigan: 15 credits (12 ULCS and 3 Expanded ULCS).

title: EECS 496 or EECS 295 (or approved alternatives)
description: A short course on professional and social responsibility in engineering and computing, such as professional ethics, teamwork, and the social impacts of technology.
notes: Choice slot: Michigan's EECS 496, EECS 295, or approved alternatives. Official EECS descriptions are in data/raw/umich/ (courses-eecs page).

title: Approved CS Capstone course
description: A culminating project course in which students, usually in teams, specify, design, build, and present a substantial computing system.
notes: Michigan footnote 3: chosen from the current list of approved capstone courses.

title: TCHNCLCM 497
description: A technical communication course taken alongside a senior design project, on writing and presenting the project's reports and documentation.
notes: Michigan's TCHNCLCM course guide was not saved (Chrome blocked the download in step 13).
